We need to generate new test cases for getTypeValidator() covering untested scenarios. Existing tests cover two cases: when validators null (lazy loading triggers getValidators) and when validators already initialized (no call). Need other combos: maybe validators null but getValidators returns null (typeValidator stays null). Also when getValidators throws exception? Not likely. Could test that after lazy loading, validators becomes non-null and typeValidator set accordingly. Also test that subsequent calls after lazy loading still not call getValidators again. Also test concurrency? maybe not.

Also test that if getValidators sets validators but does not set typeValidator (i.e., typeValidator remains null). Then getTypeValidator returns null. Ensure method returns null correctly.

Also test that when validators already set but typeValidator null (maybe validators loaded but typeValidator not set). According to code, getTypeValidator just returns typeValidator; it doesn't compute. So should return null. So test that scenario.

Also test that getTypeValidator does not modify validators list (i.e., does not add). Hard.

Define a test subclass of JsonSchema overriding getValidators to control behavior.

Group names: "validators null – getValidators returns null", "validators non-null but typeValidator null", "multiple calls after lazy loading – getValidators invoked only once", "validators null – getValidators sets validators but not typeValidator", maybe "typeValidator already set with non-null validators – getTypeValidator returns existing instance".

But some overlap with existing.

Existing already test validators null and getValidators called and typeValidator set.

Existing test also validators already initialized – getValidators not called.

We need new combos:

2. validators non-null, typeValidator null – getTypeValidator returns null, getValidators not called.

3. validators null, getValidators called, but getValidators also sets validators list; ensure after call, validators non-null and typeValidator maybe set. Already partly covered but we can assert that validators list is initialized.

4. Ensure that subsequent call after lazy loading does not call getValidators again (call getTypeValidator twice). Already partially covered but we can add.

5. When getValidators throws RuntimeException – getTypeValidator propagates? Could test that exception propagates.

But may be too complex.

We'll produce groups:

- "validators null – lazy loading with getValidators not setting typeValidator"
- "validators already initialized but typeValidator null – no lazy loading"
- "multiple getTypeValidator calls after lazy loading – getValidators called only once"
- "validators null – getValidators throws exception – exception propagates"

Provide cases accordingly.
